The change bumps the manifest to schema_version 4 while the WebUI consumer (per the diff's own plan-review record, external finding 7) still pins `knownMax` at 3 — a v4 manifest reaches it only through the unsupported-version fail-soft path, which is "degrades without crashing," not "accepts." The new `test-traceability-4.0.json` contract fixture is the input for a WebUI pin, but no WebUI-side reader/schema/type update ships here.
findings.suggestion: Either land the WebUI reader update (contract pin to 4.0, `knownMax`/types accepting `acs` and `testLink.ac_id`) in the coordinated change set, or record explicit evidence that the WebUI PR exists and cites this fixture. Absent that, AC#3 cannot be marked done.

findings.file: plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/lib/collectors/test_links.py:155 (file_hit call site) and shared/scripts/lib/fr_tag_grammar.py:165 (`canonical_fr_ac` in parse_python)
findings.finding: AC existence is never validated anywhere in the pipeline. A syntactically valid tag like `covers("FR-06.01/AC99")` on a requirement that has no AC99 (typo, or stale ordinal after an AC renumber — the exact drift failure mode the plan review flagged as high severity) is silently filed as an `acs.AC99` node, manufacturing coverage for a criterion that does not exist. Notably, the new test fixture's spec (`_AC_SPEC` in test_test_links_ac_nodes.py) declares zero ACs, so every AC in the test suite is an orphan and everything still passes — the tests cannot detect this class of bug. The diff claims deferral to P3.4/P3.6, but that deferral is not in this spec section's scope, and the deferral directly contradicts the fail-closed principle applied everywhere else in this grammar (a malformed `/AC7x` invalidates the whole tag; a nonexistent `/AC99` is accepted).
findings.suggestion: Cross-check each `hit.ac_id` against the minted AC set for the resolved FR (the P3.1 `ac_identity` machinery), and emit an invalid-tag record or orphan rather than an `acs` node for unknown AC ids. At minimum, gate it in the same P3.2 change rather than deferring.

findings.finding: The test is vacuous for its stated purpose: `["AC07", "AC09"]` sorts identically under lexical and numeric ordering. A regression that swaps the sort to plain `sorted()` (the exact bug the `int(a[2:])` key in `build_requirement_nodes` guards against — "AC10" < "AC9" as strings) still passes this test. The implementation comment even names AC10/AC9 as the motivating case, but no fixture exercises it.
findings.suggestion: Change one tag in the fixture to `AC10` (e.g., `FR-06.01/AC10` instead of `AC09`) and assert the order is `["AC07", "AC10"]`, which lexical sort would reorder to `["AC07", "AC10"]`… pick values that actually diverge, e.g. `AC09` and `AC10`, asserting `["AC09", "AC10"]` fails under lexical sort.

findings.finding: The spec explicitly requires the committed frozen manifest to be regenerated ("bump it versioned"), but no updated `test-traceability.json` appears in this diff. Meanwhile `_group_d_manifest.py` (`MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION = 4`) and `_rtm_layer_columns.py` (`_SCHEMA_VERSION = 4`) now reject the still-v3 committed manifest: audit group D degrades to SKIP and RTM layer columns render "—" on this very repo until a regen lands. The risk_recheck metadata (26 changed files) suggests the regen may be in the full change set, but it is not reviewable here.
findings.suggestion: Confirm the committed manifest regen (schema_version 4, with at least one real `acs` node) is part of this same merge; if it lands separately, the two must not be split across CI-gating commits, or this repo's own compliance gate goes red/SKIP in between.

findings.finding: A TS/JS tag like `// @covers FR-01.11/AC07` binds at FR granularity with the AC silently dropped (ac_id stays None) — the same source tag produces different manifest semantics depending on language. This is documented as a known limitation, but it means the manifest can under-report AC coverage with no `invalid_tags`/`orphans` signal, which contradicts the "never a silent partial match" rule the Python path enforces for the same string.
findings.suggestion: If AC tags in TS/JS are out of scope, consider recording a TS/JS tag carrying a `/ACnn`-shaped suffix as an invalid tag (or an explicit known-limitation entry in the manifest) so the omission is visible rather than silent.  Positive notes: the bare-FR back-compat path is well tested (`test_pytest_marker_bare_fr_still_resolves_with_no_ac`, `test_bare_fr_tag_creates_no_ac_node_but_still_covers_the_fr`); MODEL_VERSION/schema_version/contract pins are bumped together with a lock-step test; the merged bare+AC same-test dedup case is covered with real assertions; and the v4 contract fixture demonstrably contains a non-empty `acs` map, closing the plan-review's "fixture doesn't exercise new fields" concern.

findings.finding: The diff bumps the producer contract to v4, but contains no Shipwright WebUI reader change or reader-level test. Acceptance criterion “The WebUI reader accepts v4” is therefore unimplemented; an existing v3-pinned reader will still treat valid v4 manifests as unsupported.
findings.suggestion: Update the WebUI’s supported manifest version and its manifest types/schema for `requirements..acs` and `testLink.ac_id`, with a v4 fixture-based reader test.

findings.finding: Parent-level deduplication keys only on `(test id, tag_source)`, so a test tagged with two ACs for the same FR, e.g. `covers("FR-06.01/AC07", "FR-06.01/AC09")`, collapses to one parent `testLink` and retains only whichever `ac_id` was encountered first. The per-AC buckets are both populated, but the top-level link inaccurately represents the source tags.
findings.suggestion: Include `ac_id` in the deduplication identity for AC-scoped links, or define and implement a representation that can preserve all AC bindings without discarding one.  Overall: ship-with-fixes. The core grammar and v4 producer are implemented and tested, but the required WebUI consumer update is absent and multi-AC tags lose parent-level provenance.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
